patient_information: A 6-year-old Malawian boy described as thin but not malnourished.
chief_complaint: Painless, proptosed left eye for 3 weeks.
history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with a painless, proptosed left eye that his family first noticed 3 weeks prior to presentation. The condition had worsened rapidly, although his vision was still normal. He denied any pain in the eye.
exposure_and_epidemiology: The patient is from the lakeshore of Lake Malawi and resides in an area endemic for malaria and schistosomiasis. Endemic Burkitt's lymphoma is noted to be the most common childhood cancer in areas where malaria is holoendemic.
physical_exam: The right eye was normal. The left eye was proptosed but non-pulsating. The left pupil was round, clear, and responded well to light. The left eyeball demonstrated significantly limited movement when he was asked to follow an object. No other swellings or abnormalities were noted.
labs_and_diagnostics: An urgent full work-up was performed to confirm the diagnosis, including a fine-needle aspirate (FNA), bone marrow aspirate (BMA), full blood count (FBC), lumbar puncture (LP), HIV antibody test, stool and urine microscopy, and an abdominal scan. The specific results of these investigations are not detailed in the text.
differential_diagnosis: The primary differential diagnosis was Burkitt’s lymphoma, given the rapid development of proptosis in a boy from a malaria-endemic area. Other considerations included another type of B cell lymphoma and rhabdomyosarcoma. Retinoblastoma was considered less likely due to the patient's age. Infection was excluded by the painless nature of the process, and an arteriovenous malformation was deemed unlikely as the mass was non-pulsating.
management_and_clinical_course: The patient was started on oral allopurinol and hyperhydration. During a lumbar puncture, he received intrathecal methotrexate and hydrocortisone as prophylaxis against CNS involvement. Chemotherapy was initiated the following day. The proptosis improved within 48 hours and was back to normal within a week. He completed four courses of chemotherapy over 30 days. A year later, he was free of disease and pronounced cured.
final_diagnosis: The final diagnosis is endemic Burkitt's lymphoma. This diagnosis was made based on the classic clinical presentation of a rapidly progressive, painless proptosis in a young boy from a malaria-holoendemic region. Although a diagnostic workup including a fine-needle aspirate was performed, the diagnosis was strongly supported by the dramatic and rapid clinical response to chemotherapy, which was initiated urgently to prevent irreversible eye damage.
